included: resources, resource templates, prompts, and completions
finite SSE progress and request-scoped logging

strengths.MUST: Normative requirement in the pinned upstream source.
strengths.SHOULD: Normative upstream recommendation exercised by this profile.
strengths.PROFILE_MUST: Release or security gate chosen by this project where upstream is optional, recommended, or silent.

requirements.assertion: Accept only JSON-RPC 2.0 request objects whose id is a string or integer; null is not a valid request id.
Every readable request id is echoed with its original JSON type and value in either the result or error response; an unreadable id is omitted from the error response.
Invalid JSON returns Parse error -32700, an invalid JSON-RPC request object returns Invalid Request -32600, and error codes are integers.
Each POST body contains one JSON-RPC request or notification, never a batch or a JSON-RPC response sent toward the server.
A notification has no id and is never represented as a request with a null id; an accepted notification receives no JSON-RPC response.

Reject client-to-server notifications on this HTTP profile before request dispatch because the 2026 core defines none; cancellation is expressed by closing the response stream. The exact HTTP error/code is reference-observed because the source permits an HTTP error with an optional id-less JSON-RPC body.
Every request params._meta contains io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities; missing required metadata returns HTTP 400 and -32602.
clientInfo is optional, self-reported metadata; requests without it succeed, and it is not used for protocol behavior or security decisions.
A request that needs an undeclared client capability returns HTTP 400 and -32021 with data.requiredCapabilities as a ClientCapabilities object.
An unknown or unsupported version returns HTTP 400 and -32022 with data.requested and data.supported; supported requests are processed independently without a negotiation handshake.
server/discover is implemented as an RPC method and returns resultType, supportedVersions, and the capabilities actually implemented by this server.
Server identity, when supplied, is placed at result._meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo'] with name and version; it is not a top-level result field and is not a security input.
A complete discovery result includes ttlMs as a non-negative integer and cacheScope as public or private.
Discovery is optional for clients: tools/list and tools/call succeed as the first RPC when their request metadata is valid.
A server advertising tools responds to tools/list with the tools currently available to that authenticated request; the list may be empty but does not vary by connection state.
Unchanged tool sets are returned in deterministic order.
Every catalog entry has a name and a valid, non-null object-root inputSchema; optional outputSchema and annotations are preserved exactly.
Every complete tools/list result includes resultType, tools, ttlMs, and cacheScope.
If pagination is implemented, cursors are opaque, an absent nextCursor means the end, and invalid cursors return -32602; an unpaginated implementation omits nextCursor.

applicability.reason: This implementation is unpaginated, so omission of nextCursor is the active branch.

requirements.assertion: tools/call requires params._meta and params.name; arguments, when present, is an object and remains absent when omitted rather than being silently rewritten to null.
Validate schemas and tool inputs using their declared dialect, defaulting to JSON Schema 2020-12; support composition and bounds, and never dereference network $ref values by default.
Execute a valid tool invocation and return content plus optional structuredContent; structuredContent may be any JSON value and must conform to outputSchema when one is declared.
Return a content array containing schema-valid text, image, audio, resource-link, or embedded-resource blocks without double-encoding JSON.
Mutation scenarios compare backend execution counts and state; the runner never retries a call implicitly and a repeated request id is not an idempotency guarantee.
Every result includes resultType; complete is used for final tool/list/discovery results and unknown result types are never emitted without an advertised extension.
Unknown tools and malformed tool requests are JSON-RPC protocol errors; tool/API/business failures are CallToolResult values with resultType complete, content, and isError true.

An unknown tool name or params that fail the CallToolRequest protocol schema return -32602; once a request structurally identifies a registered tool, failure against that tool's declared input schema is an actionable result with isError true.
CallToolResult always contains content; isError may be absent and then means false, while missing fields and explicit null remain distinguishable wherever the schema permits both.

source.section: Protocol contract and requirement IDs / P06 and P09

requirements.assertion: Expected domain and downstream API failures return complete tool-error results. Output-schema violations also return a safe tool-error result and discard invalid handler content and structuredContent. An unhandled handler exception returns sanitized -32603 with only a correlation id. No path exposes raw arguments, private output, stack traces, or secrets.
Expose one MCP endpoint that accepts POST; a conforming request advertises both application/json and text/event-stream in Accept, and this profile returns one application/json response object.

Reject a request whose media type is not application/json. The upstream transport describes a JSON POST body but does not assign a canonical status/code for this case, so the differential fixture records the pinned reference observation.

Every profile request includes MCP-Protocol-Version equal to body metadata; missing/malformed/mismatched headers return HTTP 400 and -32020, while an equal but unsupported version returns HTTP 400 and -32022.

source.section: Standard Request Headers and Server Validation

requirements.assertion: Mcp-Method is present on every request and equals body method; Mcp-Name is present on tools/call and equals params.name after decoding. Header names compare case-insensitively and values case-sensitively. Validation failures return HTTP 400 and -32020.
Non-ASCII, unsafe, padded, control-containing, and sentinel-looking Mcp-Name or Mcp-Param values use the exact =?base64?<UTF-8 base64>?= encoding and are decoded before comparison.

x-mcp-header names are non-empty RFC 9110 tokens, unique case-insensitively, apply only to statically reachable string/integer/boolean properties, and never expose sensitive fields; invalid registered schemas fail before serving.

Each non-null annotated argument requires its matching Mcp-Param header and must equal the decoded body value; absent/null arguments omit it. Invalid characters, missing headers, or mismatches return HTTP 400 and -32020.
An RPC method the server does not implement returns HTTP 404 with -32601 and the readable request id; this includes optional methods whose capabilities were not advertised.

Reject a request whose Accept header does not advertise both application/json and text/event-stream. Upstream states the client requirement but does not assign a canonical server status/code, so the differential fixture records the pinned reference observation.
Process each request only from its own metadata, credentials, and explicit identifiers; never infer version, capabilities, identity, tenant, task, or conversation from a connection or prior request.
The 2026 profile has no initialize handshake or MCP transport session and does not expose legacy session GET/DELETE behavior.
Validate Origin when present and return HTTP 403 for a disallowed origin; local samples bind to loopback.

source.section: JSON Schema Usage / Composition-Keyword Resource Use

requirements.assertion: Bound schema depth, subschema count, remote-reference behavior, and validation time so malicious schemas cannot exhaust the validator.
Validate tool inputs, enforce access controls, rate-limit calls, and sanitize outputs.

source.section: Protocol contract and requirement IDs / P09

requirements.assertion: Reject oversized or excessively deep bodies before execution, use bounded processing, emit Retry-After for rate limiting, and never log tokens, raw private arguments, or private output.

Authenticate and authorize discovery, listing, and execution independently on every request; missing, invalid, expired, revoked, wrong-audience, or insufficient credentials are rejected with the host's canonical 401/403 behavior.

source.section: Access Token Usage and Error Handling

requirements.assertion: Bearer tokens are accepted only from the Authorization header, validated for this resource/audience, never accepted from the query string, and invalid tokens receive HTTP 401 while insufficient permissions receive HTTP 403 with the appropriate challenge.
Parallel principals and tenants receive only their authorized catalogs and results; a changed or revoked credential takes effect on the next request and a stale catalog never authorizes a call.

source.section: Cache Scope Field and Security Considerations

requirements.assertion: Protected or authorization-filtered discovery/catalog results use cacheScope private and are never reused across authorization contexts; cache hints never replace authorization.
Validate the inbound token before processing or returning data, require the server as its audience, and never pass the caller's token through to an upstream API.
Advertise tools as tools:{} and omit listChanged unless the corresponding notification behavior is implemented.
Do not advertise optional capabilities or extensions that are not implemented; unsupported extension behavior falls back to core behavior or fails explicitly.
Calls to genuinely unknown, legacy, or unadvertised optional methods fail deterministically with Method not found -32601 rather than accidental handler exposure.
Apply configurable per-request timeouts and an absolute maximum timeout even when progress is observed.
Closing an SSE stream cancels that request, stops work as soon as practical, sends no later messages, and releases bounded subscription capacity.

source.section: Equality rules and Initial scenario inventory / state

requirements.assertion: A timeout does not promise rollback, and neither server nor runner retries a mutation automatically; timeout-after-commit and an explicit repeated call are observed as separate cases with execution counts.
Advertise resources and return the authorization-filtered resource catalog with the pinned descriptor, caching, and pagination shape.
List resource templates with valid RFC 6570 templates and pinned descriptor, caching, and pagination fields.
Authorize and resolve static or templated resources per invocation and return schema-valid text or binary contents.
Return Invalid Params -32602 with the requested URI for a missing resource, never an ambiguous empty contents array.
Advertise prompts and return the authorization-filtered prompt catalog with required argument metadata and private caching.
Resolve prompt arguments per invocation and return schema-valid prompt messages and content.
Validate required prompt arguments before execution and return Invalid Params -32602 when they are missing.
Advertise completions and return at most 100 schema-valid string suggestions with consistent total and hasMore metadata.

Return InputRequiredResult only from supported methods, require inputRequests or opaque requestState, validate declared capabilities, and bind protected continuation state to caller, request, arguments, and expiry.
Validate elicitation results against the frozen requested schema, ignore unknown response keys, reject tampered state, and replay completed continuations without duplicate effects.
Accept valid multiple or partial input responses and re-request every still-missing or invalid response instead of failing the request.
Emit finite progress notifications only for the requesting active token, monotonically before the terminal response, and emit no independent server request.
Emit schema-valid request-scoped log notifications only when the request opts into a log level and before that request terminal response.
Acknowledge subscriptions first, bind every notification to the subscription ID and caller, and enforce exact tool, prompt, resource-list, and resource-URI filters across concurrent streams.

source.section: Capability negotiation, polymorphic results, and task creation

requirements.assertion: Advertise the Tasks extension, require per-request client opt-in for required tools, and return an opaque strongly visible working task only after durable creation.
Keep task state bounded and caller-bound, authorize every access, expose only the status-specific inline payload, retain it through TTL, and never retry task mutations automatically.
A completed task contains the validated final result of the original operation; tool-level isError remains completed while JSON-RPC failures use failed with error.
Expose all outstanding unique task input requests, accept valid partial updates, ignore unknown or already-satisfied keys, and acknowledge updates with an empty complete result.
Acknowledge tasks/cancel with an empty complete result and cooperatively stop or mark the bound in-progress task cancelled without using notifications/cancelled.

evidencePolicy.wireCases: Checked-in interop/fixtures/wire-cases.json IDs with reciprocal exact requirement tags.
evidencePolicy.jvmTests: Fully qualified JUnit class and method names in checked-in Java test sources.
evidencePolicy.officialChecks: Exact check IDs in the pinned @modelcontextprotocol/conformance package.
evidencePolicy.inventoryOnly: Planned or illustrative scenario names; never counted as executable evidence.
evidencePolicy.openGaps: Known missing assertions. Applicable MUST and PROFILE_MUST requirements cannot pass the evidence gate while this list is non-empty.
